digest.component_or_area: workflow step registration and seam tests
propositions: Unregistered workflow steps cannot be statically caught because registration happens as an import side effect into a process-global STEP_REGISTRY, and deletion of the import chain would silently break workflows at runtime only.

Existing seam guards fail to detect registration defects because test assertions run in-process after other tests have pre-populated STEP_REGISTRY, making the guard blind to missing imports regardless of test ordering.

Two production files (plan_review/workflow_ops.py at 794 LOC and llm/config.py at 793 LOC) lack headroom assertions while two others (gate_dispatch.py and orchestrator.py) have them, creating asymmetric structural defense against module regrowth.

The assertion message in test_gate_dispatch_seam.py references finalize_verdict call sites that no longer exist in gate_dispatch.py (now zero sites) after Change 1484 moved them to plan_review_recovery.py (three sites) and plan_review/workflow_ops.py (two sites).

Gate-YAML resolution of workflow step names (gates/plan-review.yaml:136) depends on runtime WorkflowError and the linter skips validation for unknown steps by design, leaving no static enforcement that schema references actually exist in the registry.
